title: Lapita settlers reach Fiji
description: Austronesian voyagers of the Lapita culture, makers of distinctive pottery, become the first people to settle Fiji.

title: Tasman sights Fiji
description: Abel Tasman sights the northern islands of the group on his way back to Batavia, the first European to see Fiji.

title: Bligh's open boat crosses Fiji
description: Cast adrift by the Bounty mutineers, William Bligh sails an overloaded open boat through the group, pursued by canoeists, on his way to Timor.

title: Methodist missionaries arrive
description: David Cargill and William Cross land at Lakeba and begin the mission that converts most of Fiji to Christianity within a generation.

title: Wilkes expedition surveys Fiji
description: A United States exploring squadron under Charles Wilkes charts the islands and burns two villages on Malolo after islanders kill two of its officers.

title: Cakobau accepts Christianity
description: Cakobau, the most powerful chief in Fiji, is baptised and orders his people to follow, breaking the old religion.

title: Battle of Kaba
description: Backed by Tongan canoes, Cakobau crushes his last rebel rivals, making the small island of Bau dominant in Fiji.

title: Polynesia Company land deal
description: Cakobau grants 200,000 acres around Suva to an Australian company in return for paying the debt for which American gunboats were pressing him; the settlement is the seed of modern Suva.

title: Kingdom of Fiji proclaimed
description: Cakobau becomes constitutional king of a united Fiji with ministries and a flag, the first attempt at a national government.

title: Cession to Britain
description: Cakobau and twelve other chiefs sign the Deed of Cession, and Fiji becomes a British colony without a shot being fired.

title: First Indian labourers arrive
description: The ship Leonidas lands the first 498 indentured labourers from India, the start of the girmit system that transforms Fiji's population.

title: Capital moved to Suva
description: The colonial government moves from cramped Levuka to Suva, which grows into the largest city of the Pacific islands.

title: Indian indenture ends
description: The last labour contracts are cancelled under pressure from Indian nationalists, ending the girmit system that had brought about 60,000 Indians to Fiji.

title: Independence
description: Fiji becomes independent with Ratu Sir Kamisese Mara as prime minister, ninety-six years to the day after cession.

title: Rabuka's first coup
description: Lieutenant Colonel Sitiveni Rabuka overthrows the elected government in the name of ethnic Fijian power; a second coup in September makes Fiji a republic.

title: George Speight coup
description: George Speight and gunmen seize parliament and hold the government hostage for 56 days in the name of indigenous rights.

title: Bainimarama coup
description: Commodore Frank Bainimarama overthrows the Qarase government, Fiji's fourth coup in twenty years.

title: New constitution
description: A new constitution does away with race-based voting and guarantees equal citizenship, clearing the way for elections.

title: First election since the coup
description: Bainimarama's FijiFirst party wins a majority and he stays on as an elected prime minister.

title: Cyclone Winston
description: The strongest cyclone yet recorded in the southern hemisphere kills 44 people and damages or destroys tens of thousands of homes.
